abstract: Height-two Collatz bands define finite source-residue families whose component choices depend on terminal completion counts and whose trajectories can genuinely merge. We prove an effective power saving for their averaged nearby-source overlap while retaining both features. Fix a phase and endpoint box with slope $\log_2 3\leq\lambda\leq5/3$, binary precision $T$, and $N$ source residues. For $k=\lceil\log_2 L\rceil$, let $N_t$ be the actual number of extendible prefixes at a specified common-clock cut $k+2\leq t\leq k+6$. If $T\geq2k+32$, then $N^{-1}\sum_{0<|h|<L}|R\cap(R-h)|\leq2^{12}N_tL^{-1/3200}$, improving the elementary bound $N_t-1$. We derive a two-state component law and use its exact terminal weights to give every allowed group word a uniformly positive conditional probability. An adapted integer pair state classifies all groups with no survival loss: every such group ends with equal count states, with one explicit affine exception. Sparse scalar correction histories are then controlled by an endpoint-fiber envelope, including zero-gap fusion mass. A weighted mass split yields the theorem and a translated second-moment bound. Five fixed exact-arithmetic jobs check the finite tables, probabilities and existing merger identities. An independent peer replay covers the finite algebra but not the global estimates. The result does not improve a specified-interval count, control phase unions or higher moments, or exclude a new class of integer cycles.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Averaged overlap bounds for height-two Collatz bridges with mergers
